skill.description: Designs and evaluates email A/B, multivariate, send-time, and hold-out experiments using explicit hypotheses, powered samples, guardrails, and owner-approved decision rules.
skill.summary: Build rigorous email experiment plans and interpret completed test results.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: All 57 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, metadata URLs, decimal notation, or relative documentation links. No injection or exfiltration intent appears; the residual concern is optional, consent-based persistence of experiment details.

remediation.issue: Optional memory persistence can retain campaign metrics.
remediation.suggestion: Save only after explicit approval, omit subscriber-level data and identifiers, and retain only aggregate statistics needed for future experiments.

content.value_statement: Email tests often produce weak conclusions because designs are underpowered or change several variables. This skill creates rigorous plans and interprets results with uncertainty.
actual_capabilities: Selects A/B, multivariate, send-time, or hold-out modes from the experiment goal.
Writes falsifiable hypotheses and variant matrices that isolate the tested variable.
Plans sample size, minimum detectable effect, duration, power, and read dates.
Defines primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics for each experiment.
Interprets completed exports using effect sizes, intervals, significance, and practical thresholds.
Returns an undecided result when required evidence or an approved decision rule is missing.
limitations: Requires user-provided baselines, traffic estimates, or completed email platform exports.
Does not write email subjects, body copy, creative, or calls to action.
Does not replace email quality audits, compliance review, or business ownership.
Cannot make reliable winner decisions from underpowered or prematurely reviewed tests.

use_cases.title: Plan a Subject Test
use_cases.description: Create a powered subject-line experiment with one isolated change, fixed metrics, and a scheduled read date.

use_cases.title: Measure Incremental Revenue
use_cases.description: Design a randomized hold-out that measures conversion or revenue lift against a no-send control.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Completed Results
use_cases.description: Read campaign counts, report uncertainty and guardrails, and apply only a preapproved decision rule.

prompt_templates.title: Simple A/B Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B test for [single email element]. Baseline [metric] is [rate], list size is [count], and meaningful lift is [amount].
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one variable and a known baseline.

prompt_templates.title: Send-Time Experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a send-time test for [program]. Compare [times], hold content constant, and use [metric] with baseline [rate] and volume [count].
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare deployment times without content confounding.

prompt_templates.title: Multivariate Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [factor count] multivariate email test for [factors]. Check power for every cell using baseline [rate], volume [count], and MDE [amount].
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate whether available traffic supports several cells.

prompt_templates.title: Governed Results Read-Out
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this completed export for [mode]. Report effects, intervals, significance, practical thresholds, guardrails, sample completion, and apply this owner-approved rule: [rule].
prompt_templates.scenario: Interpret results under precommitted statistical and business rules.

output_examples.input: Design a subject-line test with a 38% open baseline, 12,000 recipients, and a three-point minimum lift.
output_examples.output: Mode: A/B subject test. The plan defines control and variant cells, open rate as primary, deliverability guardrails, required sample, duration, and read date.

output_examples.input: Review delivered, click, and conversion counts for two variants without a decision rule.
output_examples.output: The read-out compares effects and intervals, checks practical and statistical thresholds, reports guardrails, and returns decision: UNDECIDED.

output_examples.input: Create a hold-out study for incremental revenue from a retention campaign.
output_examples.output: The design randomizes send and no-send groups, sizes on the conversion baseline, and uses revenue per recipient as the business outcome.

best_practices: Provide a recent baseline, daily sendable volume, and the smallest effect worth detecting.
Precommit alpha, power, sample size, read date, guardrails, and decision ownership before launch.
Keep content and audience constant when testing send time, and keep a control in every design.
anti_patterns: Do not change several email elements in one A/B variant.
Do not stop early because preliminary results appear favorable.
Do not declare a winner when the sample, guardrails, owner, or decision rule is missing.

faq.question: Which experiment modes are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports A/B, multivariate, send-time, and randomized hold-out experiments.

faq.question: What inputs are required for a new design?
faq.answer: Provide the test goal, baseline rate, list size or daily volume, and minimum meaningful lift.

faq.question: Can it analyze completed campaign results?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide per-variant delivered counts and outcome counts from your own export.

faq.question: Does it decide which variant to launch?
faq.answer: Only when a named owner supplied a precommitted action rule. Otherwise it returns an undecided result.

faq.question: Does it write the email creative?
faq.answer: No. It designs the experiment and reads results, but it does not create subjects, copy, or calls to action.

faq.question: How does it handle small lists?
faq.answer: It recommends a larger detectable effect, longer collection, fewer cells, lower power, or no test.
